16 amu is the approximate atomic mass of oxygen, not the molecular mass of water.
Molecular mass is the sum of the atomic masses: 2(1) + 16 = 18 amu.
18 g is the mass of one mole of water, not the molecular mass of one molecule.
The molecular mass of H₂O is 18 amu.
The K shell is the first shell and can hold a maximum of 2 electrons.
Eight electrons is the maximum capacity of the L shell.
Eighteen electrons is the maximum capacity of the M shell.
Thirty-two electrons is the maximum capacity of the N shell.

Potassium has lower ionization energy than sodium and lithium.
Sodium has lower ionization energy than lithium.
Ionization energy increases up Group 1, so lithium has the highest value among these choices.

NaCl consists of sodium and chloride ions, so it is ionic.
C₆H₁₂O₆ is a molecular covalent compound.

CH₄ has single covalent bonds.

C₂H₄ has a carbon–carbon double bond.
240°C is not the stated transition temperature for phosphorus in this syllabus.

260°C is above the stated transition temperature.
270°C is above the stated transition temperature.
A dental amalgam is not a liquid dissolved in another liquid.
Mercury, which is liquid, is mixed with solid metals to form an amalgam, making it a liquid-in-solid solution.
A solid-in-liquid solution has a solid solute in a liquid solvent, unlike dental amalgam.
Dental amalgam is not classified as a solid-in-solid solution.
Paint is commonly given as an example of a suspension.
Jelly is a gel, a type of colloid.
Starch dispersions are generally classified as colloids rather than suspensions in this context.
Albumin forms a colloidal solution, not a suspension.
Acetic acid is a weak acid and only partially ionizes in water.
Sodium hydroxide is a strong base and dissociates essentially completely in aqueous solution.
Benzene is a molecular compound that does not ionize in water.
Sugar dissolves as molecules and does not ionize in water.
Lithium is the least electropositive of these alkali metals because electropositivity increases down Group 1.
Sodium is more electropositive than lithium.
Potassium is more electropositive than sodium and lithium.
Rubidium is more electropositive than the other listed metals.
Sodium is soft and can be shaped, so it is not the least malleable choice here.

Gold is highly malleable.
Silver is highly malleable.
Hydrogen has the lowest molar mass among these gases and diffuses fastest.

Chlorine is much heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
Fluorine is heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
KBr is soluble in water.
NaCl is soluble in water.

MgCl₂ is soluble in water.

H⁺ accepts electrons and is reduced to H₂, so it is the oxidizing agent.
H₂ is the product of reduction, not the oxidizing agent.
